search_log: Searched "Gray Mountain John Grisham excerpt first chapter publisher" and opened the author, Hachette/Penguin, Bookreporter, and Google Books results.
Searched "Gray Mountain John Grisham third person narrator point of view" and opened the explicit BookRags point-of-view analysis.
Searched exact opening text, including "The horror was in the waiting," which located and confirmed the authorized English excerpt on John Grisham's site.

Searched "Gray Mountain alternating narration multiple narrators," "epistolary diary frame narrative," and narrator/omniscient variants; found no evidence of sustained first- or second-person base sections.
Google Books exposed bibliographic data and a section list but not usable sustained prose in the opened page, so it was retained only as a research dead end rather than evidence.
Targeted exact-quote searches showed that q03262 is letter-like embedded material and did not reveal any whole-book first-person structure.
person_note: The quote set repeatedly supplies sustained, externally narrated scenes centered on Samantha Kofer and other characters, while the authorized English and Spanish openings independently show the same third-person base. The whole-book point-of-view description confirms that the dominant mode is third-person limited to Samantha, with brief omniscient shifts that remain third person. First-person forms in dialogue, quoted thought, and the embedded message at q03262 are local material, not autonomous base sections. Some clipped passages retain uncertain quotation boundaries, but none provides credible evidence of alternating person; the remaining uncertainty is limited to those local fragments, not the book-level classification.
